thread.title: Nutanix Stock Rebounds As Google Networking Competition Worries Ease | Investor's Business Daily

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Nutanix Stock Rebounds As Google Networking Competition Worries Ease | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Nutanix stock bounced back on Tuesday, a day after worries that Google would sell competing products spurred a sell-off in the company's shares.
X Shares in cloud computing software company Nutanix ( NTNX ) jumped 6.9% to close at 49.65 on the stock market today . Shares in Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google edged up 0.6% to 1,167.11. Nutanix stock plunged 11.5% on Monday.
Digital media outlet The Information reported on Monday that Google's cloud computing unit is trialing rival devices. They combine server, storage and networking in a few large customers' private-cloud data centers. The report said Google has not yet decided if it will sell them as commercial products.
That could pose a threat to Nutanix's software, which manages network, storage and server infrastructure in private cloud-computing platforms. It's all part of an emerging market called "hyperconvergence."

Please contact customer service CLOSE Most of the large technology and internet companies — including Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Google — develop in-house chips and other gear for internal data centers.
Tech Giants Develop Data Center Technology "Our view is that similar to Amazon Web Services and Microsoft, we're not surprised to see Google show interest in private-cloud infrastructure, but believe partnering with vendors such as Nutanix could make it easier," RBC Capital analyst Matthew Hedberg said in a note to clients.
William Blair analyst Jason Ader said in his report: "If Google were to decide to enter the HCI market more broadly, the company would have a long way to go to establish itself in the enterprise against entrenched players like Nutanix and VMware ( VMW )."
With Tuesday's rebound, Nutanix stock has gained 126% from a year ago. However, Nutanix stock is down from a 12-month high of 62.58 set on June 14.
The Nutanix sell-off was similar to that of computer networking companies in July, prompted by a report involving Amazon. Shares of Cisco Systems ( CSCO ), Juniper Networks ( JNPR ) and Arista Networks ( ANET ) tumbled on a report that AWS would sell network data switches.
Amazon denied such plans and the networking stocks rebounded.
